answer: Staked bonding makes each sybil identity expensive. A new agent must lock a refundable deposit that is slashed if its peers flag it for fabricated work. Picture a glacier of collateral: each identity sits on it, and cheap clones can never melt through to the nadir of trust. Peers attest only after an agent's output passes a challenge, and a trellis of vouching links ties newcomers to established members. An attacker who wants 50 fake agents must post 50 bonds and win 50 vouches, so the cost is real money plus weeks of earned reputation.
